meta.instrument: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 - as amended upto March 12, 2025
meta.authored: Read from the held text, provision by provision. NOT generated from master sheet.xlsx - unlike pit_master.json, ca_master.json and lodr_*.json, which build_master.py and build_lodr.py generate from the owner's spreadsheet and which must not be hand-edited. This file is hand-authored against reference/ and every rule carries the words it came from in `quote`.
meta.scope: ONLY the obligations this regulation places on a LISTED COMPANY. PIT binds several different parties and this is the one that matters: Chapter IIA (Reg 5A to 5H) is the mutual fund units regime and binds asset management companies and trustees; Chapter IIIA (Reg 7A to 7M) is the informant mechanism and binds the Board and the informant, except Reg 7I and 7J which bind the employer; Reg 10, 11 and 12 are sanction, the Board's power to remove difficulties, and repeal.
meta.why: The generated corpus holds 42 rules and cites 8 of the 33 numbered provisions in the regulation body. Two different gaps were measured: whole provisions absent (Reg 6, 7I, 7J), and SUB-PROVISIONS of provisions the corpus already cites - Reg 3 has six sub-regulations and the corpus cites two; Reg 9A has seven and the corpus cites three limbs of one. In a regulation this small the duties concentrate in a few provisions with many limbs, so counting provisions alone understates what is missing.
readingNotes: Reg 5A to 5H were checked one by one and every one of them opens with 'asset management company', 'trustees' or 'units of a mutual fund'. Reg 5D alone states five periods - two working days, two trading days, sixty days, six months, two months. NONE of them is a listed company's. Loading that chapter would hand a listed issuer an AMC's obligations, which is the SS2z defect.
Reg 5H is the mutual fund mirror of Reg 9A, and Reg 5C the mirror of Reg 3. The parallel numbering is what makes the chapter dangerous to read quickly.

Reg 7I binds 'every person required to have a Code of Conduct under these regulations'. A listed company is required to have one by Reg 9(1), so it binds the company - and Reg 7I(3) makes an employer who violates the Chapter liable to penalty, debarment, suspension or criminal prosecution by the Board.
No provision number appears twice in this compilation, so the SS3z trap - a span anchored on a footnote reproducing repealed text - does not arise here. It was checked before anything was read.

overlaps.PIT-SDD-FRAMEWORK-36: The generated corpus already carries a row titled 'Structured Digital Database' reading 'Maintain an auditable digital database showing UPSI sharing/access information and preserve integrity of the information trail'. It cites NO numbered provision and states NO period. Reg 3(5) and Reg 3(6) here are that duty read from the regulation: they add the Permanent Account Number requirement, the bar on outsourcing, the two-calendar-day entry window for information from outside the organisation, and the eight-year preservation period. Where the two differ, these cite the provision and quote it.

rules.title: Share unpublished price sensitive information for a transaction only on the board's informed opinion, and publish it two trading days ahead where no open offer follows
rules.detail: Unpublished price sensitive information may be communicated, provided, allowed access to or procured in connection with a transaction only in two cases: where the transaction entails an obligation to make an open offer under the takeover regulations and the board of directors is of informed opinion that sharing the information is in the best interests of the company; or where it does not entail an open offer, the board is of that informed opinion, and the information is disseminated to be made generally available at least two trading days before the transaction is effected, in such form as the board determines to be adequate and fair to cover all relevant and material facts.
rules.quote: an unpublished price sensitive information may be communicated, provided, allowed access to or procured, in connection with a transaction that would. not attract the obligation to make an open offer under the takeover regulations but where the board of directors of the listed company is of informed opinion that sharing of such information is in the best interests of the company and the information that constitute unpublished price sensitive information is disseminated to be made generally available at least two trading days prior to the proposed transaction being effected in such form as the board of directors may determine to be adequate and fair to cover all relevant and material facts
rules.frequency: On every transaction where UPSI is shared
rules.timelineText: Generally available at least two trading days prior to the transaction being effected, where the transaction does not attract an open offer

due.when: Before UPSI is shared for a proposed transaction

rules.appliesToText: Listed company sharing unpublished price sensitive information for a proposed transaction
rules.evidence: Board resolution recording the informed opinion; the disclosure made generally available with its date and time; the form the board determined
rules.notes: TWO TRADING DAYS, and it runs BACKWARD from the transaction. Not computed: there is no exchange trading calendar here, and counting trading days as calendar days would place the deadline LATER than the regulation allows, which is the unsafe direction. Note the two limbs are different: an open-offer transaction needs the board's informed opinion and nothing more, while a transaction that attracts no open offer additionally needs the information made generally available first.

rules.title: Require the parties receiving unpublished price sensitive information to execute confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements
rules.detail: For the purposes of Reg 3(3), the board of directors must require the parties to execute agreements contracting confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations. Those parties must keep the information confidential except for the purpose of Reg 3(3), and must not otherwise trade in the securities of the company while in possession of unpublished price sensitive information.
rules.quote: For purposes of sub-regulation (3), the board of directors shall require the parties to execute agreements to contract confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations on the part of such parties and such parties shall keep information so received confidential, except for the purpose of sub-regulation (3), and shall not otherwise trade in securities of the company when in possession of unpublished price sensitive information
rules.frequency: On every transaction where UPSI is shared

due.when: Before UPSI is shared under Reg 3(3)

rules.appliesToText: Listed company sharing unpublished price sensitive information for a proposed transaction
rules.evidence: Executed confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements with every recipient; board resolution requiring them
rules.notes: The duty is on the BOARD to require the agreements, not merely to obtain them if offered. The obligation the agreement carries runs on after the transaction: the recipient may not trade in the company's securities while holding the information, whatever the transaction does.

rules.title: Maintain the structured digital database internally, with PAN, time stamping and audit trails, and enter outside information within two calendar days
rules.detail: The board of directors must ensure a structured digital database is maintained containing the nature of the unpublished price sensitive information, the names of the persons who shared it and of those with whom it was shared, together with their Permanent Account Number or another identifier authorised by law where PAN is not available. The database must not be outsourced and must be maintained internally with adequate internal controls and checks such as time stamping and audit trails to ensure it cannot be tampered with. Information not emanating from within the organisation may be entered not later than two calendar days from its receipt.
rules.quote: maintained containing the nature of unpublished price sensitive information and the names of such persons who have shared the information and also the names of such persons with whom information is shared under this regulation along with the Permanent Account Number or any other identifier authorized by law where Permanent Account Number is not available. Such database shall not be outsourced and shall be maintained internally with adequate internal controls and checks such as time stamping and audit trails to ensure non-tampering of the database. Provided that entry of information, not emanating from within the organisation, in structured digital database may be done not later than 2 calendar days from the receipt of such information
rules.timelineText: Contemporaneous; information from outside the organisation not later than 2 calendar days from receipt

due.when: On every sharing or receipt of unpublished price sensitive information

rules.appliesToText: Listed company required to handle unpublished price sensitive information
rules.evidence: The database itself, showing time stamps, audit trail and PAN for every entry; confirmation it is hosted internally
rules.notes: Three requirements here are the ones most often missed, and none of them is in the register's existing uncited 'Structured Digital Database' row: the Permanent Account Number of every person, the BAR ON OUTSOURCING - the database may not sit with a vendor - and the two calendar days for information received from outside. The two days is a maximum for external information only; information arising inside the organisation is entered contemporaneously.

rules.title: Preserve the structured digital database for not less than eight years, and longer while the Board is investigating
rules.detail: The board of directors must ensure the structured digital database is preserved for a period of not less than eight years after completion of the relevant transactions. Where any information is received from the Board about an investigation or enforcement proceeding, the relevant information in the database must be preserved until those proceedings are complete.
rules.quote: The board of directors or head(s) of the organisation of every person required to handle unpublished price sensitive information shall ensure that the structured digital database is preserved for a period of not less than eight years after completion of the relevant transactions and in the event of receipt of any information from the Board regarding any investigation or enforcement proceedings, the relevant information in the structured digital database shall be preserved till the completion of such proceedings
rules.timelineText: Not less than eight years after completion of the relevant transactions; longer while an investigation or enforcement proceeding is on foot
rules.appliesToText: Listed company required to handle unpublished price sensitive information
rules.evidence: Retention policy naming eight years; evidence the database for closed transactions is still retrievable
rules.notes: Eight years runs from COMPLETION OF THE RELEVANT TRANSACTIONS, not from the entry or from the financial year end. The register's existing 'Structured Digital Database' row says only 'preserve integrity of the information trail' and states no period at all - a Company Secretary reading that has no way to know the answer is eight years. Note also that a communication from the Board freezes deletion until the proceedings end, which can be well past the eight years.

rules.title: Maintain the insider trading disclosures for a minimum period of five years
rules.detail: The disclosures made under Chapter III - the initial and continual disclosures of trading by promoters, members of the promoter group, designated persons and directors - must be maintained by the company for a minimum period of five years, in such form as may be specified. Those disclosures must include trading by the discloser's immediate relatives and by any other person for whom the discloser takes trading decisions, and must include trading in derivatives of securities.
rules.quote: The disclosures made under this Chapter shall be maintained by the company, for a minimum period of five years, in such form as may be specified
rules.timelineText: A minimum period of five years
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company receiving disclosures under Chapter III
rules.evidence: The disclosure register with the retained forms; retention policy naming five years
rules.notes: This is the COMPANY's duty, distinct from the discloser's duty to make the disclosure. Two scoping rules travel with it and are the ones most often missed: Reg 6(2) requires the disclosures to cover trading by the discloser's immediate relatives and by any person for whom the discloser takes trading decisions, and Reg 6(3) requires them to cover trading in derivatives, with the traded value of the derivatives taken into account. Note five years here against eight years for the structured digital database under Reg 3(6) - two different retention periods in one regulation.

rules.title: Ensure the Code of Conduct protects an employee who files a Voluntary Information Disclosure Form from retaliation
rules.detail: Every person required to have a Code of Conduct under these regulations must ensure that the Code provides suitable protection against discharge, termination, demotion, suspension, threats, harassment, direct or indirect, or discrimination against any employee who files a Voluntary Information Disclosure Form - whether or not the information is accepted and whether or not a reward follows - by reason of filing it, of testifying or assisting the Board in any investigation, inquiry, audit, examination or proceeding, or of breaching a confidentiality agreement or terms of employment solely to cooperate with the Board.
rules.quote: Every person required to have a Code of Conduct under these regulations shall ensure that such a Code of Conduct provides for suitable protection against any discharge, termination, demotion, suspension, threats, harassment, directly or indirectly or discrimination against any employee who files a Voluntary Information Disclosure Form, irrespective of whether the information is considered or rejected by the Board or he or she is eligible for a Reward under these regulations
rules.frequency: Continuous; on every review of the Code
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company required to have a Code of Conduct under Reg 9
rules.evidence: The Code of Conduct clause providing the protection; board approval of the amended Code
rules.notes: A listed company is required to have a Code of Conduct by Reg 9(1), so this binds the company. It is a requirement about the CONTENT of the Code, and a Code drafted before the informant mechanism was inserted will not carry it. Reg 7I(3) makes an employer who violates this Chapter liable to penalty, debarment, suspension or criminal prosecution by the Board - so it is not a drafting nicety. 'Employee' is defined here to include a director, partner, and regular or contractual employee, but not an advocate.

rules.title: Carry no term in any agreement or in the Code of Conduct that prevents a person reporting to the Board
rules.detail: Any term in an agreement, oral or written, or in a Code of Conduct is void so far as it purports to preclude any person other than an advocate from submitting to the Board information relating to a violation of the securities laws that has occurred, is occurring, or is reasonably believed to be about to occur. No person may by threat or act impede an individual from communicating with the Board, including by enforcing or threatening to enforce a confidentiality agreement. No employer may require an employee to notify it of a Voluntary Information Disclosure Form filed with the Board, or to seek its prior permission or consent, or the guidance of anyone engaged by the employer, before or after filing.
rules.quote: Any term in an agreement (oral or written) or Code of Conduct, is void in so far as it purports to preclude any person, other than an advocate, from submitting to the Board information relating to the violation of the securities laws that has occurred, is occurring or has a reasonable belief that it would occur
rules.evidence: Employment agreements, confidentiality agreements, settlement agreements and the Code reviewed against this provision
rules.notes: This reaches further than the Code of Conduct: it voids the offending term in ANY agreement, which means employment contracts, non-disclosure agreements and settlement agreements have to be read against it. The Explanation is the operative part for most companies - an employer may not require an employee to tell it about a filing, or to ask permission first. A standard confidentiality clause that requires notification of any regulatory contact breaches this.

rules.title: The board of directors must ensure the Chief Executive Officer or Managing Director ensures compliance
rules.detail: The board of directors of every listed company must ensure that the Chief Executive Officer, the Managing Director or such other analogous person ensures compliance with Reg 9 - the codes of fair disclosure and conduct - and with Reg 9A(1) and 9A(2), the system of internal controls.
rules.quote: The board of directors of every listed company and the board of directors or head(s) of the organisation of intermediaries and fiduciaries shall ensure that the Chief Executive Officer or the Managing Director or such other analogous person ensures compliance with regulation 9 and sub-regulations (1) and (2) of this regulation
rules.evidence: Board minutes recording the oversight; the CEO or MD's confirmation of compliance placed before the board
rules.notes: A two-layer duty, and each layer is separately enforceable: Reg 9A(1) puts the internal controls on the CEO or MD, and this sub-regulation puts on the BOARD the duty of ensuring that person does it. Board minutes that record no oversight of the PIT controls do not evidence this.

rules.title: The Audit Committee must review compliance at least once in a financial year and verify the internal controls
rules.detail: The Audit Committee of a listed company must review compliance with the provisions of these regulations at least once in a financial year, and must verify that the systems for internal control are adequate and are operating effectively.
rules.quote: The Audit Committee of a listed company or other analogous body for intermediary or fiduciary shall review compliance with the provisions of these regulations at least once in a financial year and shall verify that the systems for internal control are adequate and are operating effectively
rules.timelineText: At least once in a financial year

due.cadence: At least once in a financial year

rules.evidence: Audit Committee minutes recording the review and the verification, with the date; the compliance officer's report placed before it
rules.notes: An annual Audit Committee agenda item, and the one in this supplement most likely to be missed outright because nothing files anywhere when it happens. Two distinct acts are required and minutes must show both: REVIEW compliance with the regulations, and VERIFY that the internal controls are adequate AND operating effectively. The regulation fixes the cadence and not the date, so no date is computed - it is met by an Audit Committee meeting in the year, and a company whose Audit Committee met four times has still not met it unless one of those meetings did this.

rules.title: Have board-approved procedures for inquiry into a leak of unpublished price sensitive information, and inform the Board promptly
rules.detail: Every listed company must formulate written policies and procedures for inquiry in the case of a leak, or a suspected leak, of unpublished price sensitive information, approved by the board of directors. It must initiate appropriate inquiries on becoming aware of such a leak or suspected leak, and inform SEBI promptly of the leak, the inquiries and the results of those inquiries.
rules.quote: Every listed company shall formulate written policies and procedures for inquiry in case of leak of unpublished price sensitive information or suspected leak of unpublished price sensitive information, which shall be approved by board of directors of the company and accordingly initiate appropriate inquiries on becoming aware of leak of unpublished price sensitive information or suspected leak of unpublished price sensitive information and inform the Board promptly of such leaks, inquiries and results of such inquiries
rules.frequency: Policy: continuous. Inquiry: on becoming aware of a leak
rules.timelineText: Promptly on becoming aware of a leak or suspected leak

due.when: On becoming aware of a leak or suspected leak of UPSI

rules.evidence: The board-approved leak inquiry policy; the inquiry record; the intimation sent to SEBI with its date
rules.notes: Three separate duties in one sub-regulation, and a company can hold the policy and still breach the other two: FORMULATE the written policy with board approval, INITIATE an inquiry on becoming aware, and INFORM SEBI promptly of the leak, the inquiry and its results. A SUSPECTED leak engages it - the trigger is not a proven one. 'Promptly' is not a fixed period, so no date can be computed.

rules.title: Have a whistle-blower policy and make employees aware of it
rules.detail: The listed company must have a whistle-blower policy and must make employees aware of that policy, so that they can report instances of leak of unpublished price sensitive information.
rules.quote: The listed company shall have a whistle-blower policy and make employees aware of such policy to enable employees to report instances of leak of unpublished price sensitive information
rules.evidence: The whistle-blower policy; evidence employees were made aware of it - circulation, intranet, training records, acknowledgements
rules.notes: Two limbs, and the second is the one that fails: HAVE the policy, and MAKE EMPLOYEES AWARE of it. A policy on the intranet that nobody has been told about does not satisfy the second. This is a separate requirement from the vigil mechanism under s.177(9) of the Companies Act and from the informant protection under Reg 7I - a company can hold all three obligations at once and they are not interchangeable.

rules.title: Collect the initial holding disclosure a new KMP, director or promoter owes the company within seven days of appointment or of becoming a promoter
rules.detail: THE SEVEN DAYS IS THE PERSON'S, NOT THE COMPANY'S. Reg 7(1)(b) binds "every person on appointment as a key managerial personnel or a director of the company or upon becoming a promoter or member of the promoter group", and the disclosure runs TO the listed entity. The company's duty is to collect it and to hold it -- Reg 6(4) keeps these disclosures five years -- and the exchange intimation is a separate obligation under Reg 7(2)(b), which carries its own two trading days. Claiming the seven days as the entity's own deadline would put a filing on the register that the company does not owe (SS3y's s.84, SS3z's Reg 30A). Note also that Reg 7(1)(a) -- the one-time initial disclosure owed when these regulations took effect -- was OMITTED with effect from 26 April 2021 and no longer exists.
rules.quote: Every person on appointment as a key managerial personnel or a director of the company or upon becoming a promoter or member of the promoter group shall disclose his holding of securities of the company as on the date of appointment or becoming a promoter, to the company within seven days of such appointment or becoming a promoter
rules.timelineText: Within seven days of the appointment or of becoming a promoter
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, on any appointment of a KMP or director
rules.evidence: The signed disclosure, and the date it reached the company
rules.submitTo: Received by the company; no filing
rules.notes: No date is computed: this app holds no register of appointments, so there is nothing for the seven days to run from. The period is stated regardless -- a period this app cannot compute is not a period that does not exist (SS3x).
